messages:
sara: Heads-up from ACME call: their trial workload spikes cause a repeatable p99 tail. We need a clear acceptance checklist + emergency rollback flow before Friday demo.

matt: Got the traces. At ~150 concurrent RPS we see p95 ~220ms but p99 climbs to ~900ms and occasional 504s.

anya: Yikes. Can we capture the exact request profile and which prompts trigger it? Security also wants a defensive routing statement for the demo.

matt: quick profile: ```
traffic: burst to 150 conc
model: gptx-6b-quant
p95: 220ms
p99: 900ms
timeouts: 0.8%
```

devon: Proposal for trial success: keep acceptance narrow and measurable. My recommendation: p95 <= 300ms, p99 <= 600ms under the agreed steady-state load (120 conc); weekly token spend <= $1,200; quality >= 92% on the 250 curated prompts ACME provided. If we need >120 conc for demo that's a separate pricing uplift.

anya: Security additions: must include KMS key ownership proof (customer-managed key option), E2E encryption details, and confirmation that logs are scrubbed of PII. Also ask for an explicit fallback path so ACME knows we won't lose availability.

sara: ACME expects the demo in their VPC. We promised a private demo + audit logs. That means Private checklist items must be included in acceptance.

matt: Operational fallback idea: if p99 > 650ms for 2 continuous minutes OR error rate > 1% for 1 minute, route new requests to gptx-3b-q and send alerts. Record the event in audit logs. Auto-scale attempt first (add 1 more GPU pool) for 2 minutes; if no improvement, fallback.

devon: And quality guardrails: run golden set every 5 minutes. If accuracy drops >4% vs baseline after fallback, auto-rollback to previous model and page oncall if persisted >20 minutes. Owner: matt.

anya: I'll assemble a short security appendix and a KMS verification checklist for the handoff doc. We should show how keys are rotated and where audit logs live.

sara: Timeline: finalize criteria today, run two stress windows tomorrow (10:00 and 15:00 PT) for 45 mins each, capture cost telemetry and eval results, and share a one-page decision memo to ACME by COB. Sales will not sign pilot until criteria met.

matt: I'll build the harness and a CI step that fails the run if any of the guards trip. Script snippet I'll add to repo: ```bash
# pass if all are true
[ "$P99_MS" -le 600 ] && [ "$EVAL_ACC" -ge 92 ] && [ "$WEEKLY_COST" -le 1200 ] || exit 1
```

devon: Note on pricing: if we enable burst GPUs for demo we should include a clearly marked line-item estimate. Add that to the runbook.

anya: Also request a short signed attestation from ACME on their expected max concurrency window so we can calibrate SLOs for the demo.

deploybot: deploybot: scheduled canary run at 1902242000 with 60% traffic split; will post logs to /canaries/acme-trial.

sara: Great. Action items: @matt -> harness + CI fail criteria + rollback playbook; @anya -> security appendix + KMS checklist; @devon -> runbook pricing note + burst estimate; sara -> send decision memo to ACME after tests. Reconvene 09:45 PT tomorrow to confirm readiness. :thumbsup:
